posts.heading: September 20, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 233 feeder visits, slightly exceeding the previous seven-day average of 217. With 19 species recorded, the count sits near the recent weekly mean, though the absence of the Northern Mockingbird distinguishes the day from the six prior days when it was consistently present.

American Crows continued their regular presence, appearing in the auditory record every day of the past week.

The day began with a Tufted Titmouse at the tube feeder 12 minutes before sunrise and ended with a Northern Cardinal 14 minutes after sunset.

posts.heading: September 19, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 213 feeder visits and 21 species, placing the day slightly above the previous week's average in both activity and variety. While the total count of heard detections was lower than the weekly mean, the visual activity remained consistent with recent trends, with Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees forming the bulk of the feeder traffic. The Carolina Wren dominated the audio logs with 116 detections, continuing its pattern of being present on every one of the last seven days.

The mix of species held steady compared to the previous week, with all ten daily regulars recorded. Several species appeared for the first time in the seven-day window, including a Black Vulture, a Chipping Sparrow, and an Orchard Oriole, each with a single visual record. Downy Woodpeckers, Northern House Wrens, and Brown Thrashers, which had been present earlier in the week, were absent from this day's logs.

The audio source change on September 13 and the seed feeder replacement on the same day did not introduce any new species detected by ear, as no first-time heard records were logged. The visual data remained focused on the established feeder regulars, with no new confident visual records established at the station during this period.

posts.heading: September 18, 2026
posts.text:
September 18 added up to a quiet day at the station, with 99 feeder visits significantly below the previous seven-day average of 199.7. The count of 17 species matched the weekly average, but the drop in physical traffic stood out against the 302 visits recorded on Thursday.

The subdued visitation aligns with the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which replaced an old unit that was causing bird detection problems. No new species were introduced by the audio switch to the pi-mic on September 13, and the station’s roster remained consistent with the week’s standard residents.

Mourning Doves, a regular presence for the last seven days, were absent today, as were Gray Catbirds and Northern House Wrens. The day closed with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird visiting just six minutes after sunset, marking the final visual record.

posts.heading: September 17, 2026
posts.text:
September 17 added up to one of the busiest days of the week, with 302 feeder visits and 21 species recorded against a seven-day average of roughly 170 visits. Tufted Titmice remained the dominant feeder presence, accounting for 123 of the visits, while Carolina Chickadees and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds also held steady as regulars.

The acoustic record was dominated by Carolina Wrens, which contributed 132 detections, and Northern Cardinals, with 39. Several other species, including Blue Jays and Gray Catbirds, were heard frequently, while rare visitors like the Red-shouldered Hawk and White-eyed Vireo appeared briefly. All ten species that appear daily at this station were recorded again.

Activity at the station shifted following the installation of a new seed feeder earlier in the week, which replaced a unit previously causing detection problems. This change aligns with the rise in visual records, where Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees filled the majority of visits.

posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text: The station closed out the day with 244 feeder visits and 23 species, figures that sit well above the seven-day average of 138 visits and 14 species. This high volume continues the trend established since the seed feeder was installed on September 13, replacing the unit that had been causing detection problems. Tufted Titmice remained the dominant visual presence, while Blue Jays led the acoustic record in the final hours.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text:
September 15 was the busiest day of the past week, with 278 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, exceeding the recent seven-day averages. This surge follows the installation of the new seed feeder and pi-mic microphone on September 13. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the primary visual presences, while Carolina Wrens dominated the audio logs with 126 detections.

The station logged its first confident visual records for Black-capped Chickadees and Eastern Phoebes. The daily roster included Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays, which have been recorded on all seven recent days. American Goldfinches have not appeared since earlier in the week.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text: The station’s activity outpaced the previous week’s average significantly, with 241 feeder visits and 16 species recorded compared to the prior seven-day mean of 63.6 visits and 10.0 species. This surge follows the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which resolved previous detection issues, and the switch to a new audio source the same morning. While Tufted Titmice remained the most frequent visual visitors with 97 confident sightings, Carolina Chickadees and Mourning Doves also contributed heavily to the visual counts.
